title: Schmigadoon! on Broadway #schmigadoon #schmigadoonmusical #schmigadoo...
transcript: I'm relatively indifferent about Schmigadoon existing but I cannot deny that it was a good time. It's another musical based on something else — shocker, I know. But at least with this one, the source material is musical and is about the world of musicals. I imagine this is how it works so well as a standalone piece — I've never seen the original TV series but I found this musical totally able to hold its own. It's a comedy about a couple in a pivotal point in their relationship who find themselves trapped in Schmigadoon, a town where life is a musical. The show references and satirizes classic musical tropes in a tongue-in-cheek way. Schmigadoon is the kind of place where the sun is always shining and the people are always unnervingly cheery, but the society is actually quite archaic with its traditional gender roles and outdated ideas about love. This irony is a big source of comedy, as is the surprisingly adult humor. An ensemble piece through and through, the show features a bunch of modestly sized supporting roles, but every actor makes the most of it, leaving no moment wasted. McKenzie Kurtz specifically is marvelous in this regard. My only casting quibble is Alex Brightman who is doing great work in this show, but is assuming a role that was originated by a person of color in the TV series. I'm sure plenty of people don't really care about this, but it kind of rubs me the wrong way. As far as other critiques, I found the music pretty generic despite its witty lyricism. And while the piece is successful as a comedy, it becomes a little monotonous after a while, not quite justifying its two and a half hour run time. Overall though, the show advertises itself as musical escapism, which it certainly provides. With that, another Playbill for my collection.
